Kuvitus: talvi-ilta eteisessä. Keskellä: Illustration: a winter evening in a hallway. In the middle there is a wooden front door with a brass handle on a long metal plate. From the right a hand in a red knitted sleeve reaches towards the handle, and a small bright spark flashes between the fingertip and the metal plate. On the floor there is a striped woollen rug. On the left there is a window showing a snowy night, the moon and spruces, and a radiator under the window. A woolly hat hangs on the coat rack on the wall.
Kaavakuva: kaksi vaakasuoraa levyä. Ylem: Schematic: two horizontal plates. The upper plate is positive and its potential is 200 V; the lower, negative plate is the zero, 0 V. Between the plates there are five green vertical field lines pointing down: the field is uniform. Grey dashed lines are the equipotential surfaces 150 V, 100 V and 50 V. On the left a proton, whose red force arrow points down in the direction of the field. On the right an electron, whose red force arrow points up against the field, towards the higher potential.
Kaksi kuvaa. Vasemmalla tilannekuva: kak: Two pictures. On the left the situation: two identical positive balls hang on threads from the same hook, and the threads form a V. A dashed line goes straight down from the hook, and the angle alpha is between a thread and the vertical. On the right the free-body diagram of the right-hand ball, the ball drawn as a rectangle: the weight G from the centre straight down, the tension T of the thread from the top edge along the thread obliquely up to the left towards the hook, and the electric force F s from the right edge horizontally to the right, away from the other ball. The ball is at rest, so the forces cancel each other: the vertical part of T is as large as the weight and the horizontal part as large as the electric force. The angle is drawn larger than in the task so that the arrows can be told apart.
Kuvaaja: kondensaattorin kapasitanssi C: Graph: the capacitance C of a capacitor in picofarads as a function of the plate separation d in millimetres. Seven black points at distances 1.0–6.0 mm, capacitances from 375 pF to 82 pF. A dashed curve passes through the points; it falls steeply at small distances and levels off at large ones, but does not approach zero: twice the distance does not halve the capacitance, so neither a straight line nor plain inverse proportionality fits the points.
Kuvaaja: kapasitanssi C pikofaradeina su: Graph: the capacitance C in picofarads as a function of the quantity one divided by d in the unit one per millimetre. Seven black points between 0.17 and 1.00, capacitances from 82 pF to 375 pF. A rising straight line has been fitted to the points and extended as a dashed line to the vertical axis: it crosses the vertical axis at about 22 pF and does not pass through the origin. Two points on the line are circled, (0.20, 93) and (1.00, 376), from which the slope of about 354 pF times millimetre is read.
Käsitekartta. Ylhäällä solmu: varaus syn: Concept map. At the top is the node: a charge creates an electric field, and the field exerts a force on a charge, F = q E. Four branches go down from it. Charge and force: charge Q = n e, Coulomb's law F E = k times the product of the charges divided by r squared, and the vector sum of the forces. Field and potential: uniform field U = E times d, work done by the field W = Q U and in acceleration the kinetic energy E k = one half m v squared. Capacitor: capacitance Q = C U, parallel-plate capacitor C = epsilon zero epsilon r A divided by d and energy E = one half C U squared. Components and safety: series resistor from Kirchhoff's second law, sum of delta V = 0, efficiency of a solar cell eta = P divided by G A, and current through the body I = U divided by R.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa. Vasemmalla: Schematic, not to scale. On the left a fingertip with negative charges on its surface. On the right the metal plate of the door handle, where positive charges have moved to the surface facing the finger because of induction. Between them there is an air gap of about 3 millimetres, crossed by green field lines from the plate to the finger and a bright bluish-white spark; the field is about 3 MV/m, the dielectric strength of air. Below, the calculation: the voltage U = E times d is about 9 kV, the body is a capacitor with a capacitance of about 100 pF, so the charge Q = C U is about 0.9 microcoulombs and the energy W = one half C U squared about 4 millijoules.
Kytkentäkaavio, ei lukuarvoja. Vasemmall: Circuit diagram, no numbers. On the left a voltage source with the voltage U, its positive terminal at the top. A series resistor R is connected in the upper wire. On the right an LED in the forward direction: its triangle points down, from the positive side towards the negative side, and two small arrows of light leave it. The voltage of the LED is U D. A violet current I flows from the positive terminal through the resistor and the LED back to the negative terminal.
